newsitem.title: UK: UK to introduce computerised cattle tracing system.
newsitem.headline: UK to introduce computerised cattle tracing system.

text.p: The government on Tuesday announced proposals to implement a computerised system to trace cattle movements in Great Britain.

Farm minister Douglas Hogg said in a written parliamentary answer: "The government considers that improved cattle traceability would have considerable benefit in underpinning consumer confidence in the beef market."
But Hogg said running costs, estimated at 20 to 25 million pounds a year, would be borne by the industry. The government will pay the estimated five million pound start-up costs.

All cattle born in Great Britain since July 1, 1996 have had to have a cattle passport. These will now be put in a computer database, similar to systems already in place in Northern Ireland and some European countries.

A new private sector body known as the British Cattle Movement Service would enter data on cattle movements into the database from information provided by farmers using a simple form in a "freepost" system.
Businesses such as abattoirs and livestock markets would input data electronically. Access to the database would be allowed, probably for a fee, Hogg said. -- London Newsroom +44-171-542-7768
